page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by an expansive 480 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning sits at 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and the instance operates without a dedicated hardware GPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and throughput capabilities, notably in vector-accelerated tasks supported by AMX, AVX-512, and AVX-VNNI instruction sets. PassMark testing records a strong overall CPU score of 64,146.76 alongside high results in extended instructions (59,667.63) and encryption (50,151.68). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 272.18 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression hits 35.53 GB/sec, both placing in the upper tier. Static web serving throughput reaches 61.11 GB/sec, while in-memory operations achieve 76.28 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. CPU-based prompt evaluation across small and medium LLM models shows strong throughput, though text generation on 70B parameter models drops to 2.64 tokens/sec due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a high memory-to-core ratio, large L3 cache, and 2832 GB local NVMe storage enables heavy data caching and fast temporary disk operations without remote storage latency penalties. The lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses requires additional network configuration for external access. The system is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise data processing, static content distribution, and analytics pipelines needing substantial RAM per core.
